title: Vitamin D status and ill health: a systematic review
authors: Autier P, Boniol M, Pizot C, Mullie P
population: 290 prospective cohort studies and 172 randomised trials of non-skeletal outcomes in adults
funder: not stated in the abstract; the full text was not accessible (HTTP 403 at the publisher), so the funding statement was not read.
result: Most prospective studies reported moderate to strong inverse associations between 25-hydroxyvitamin D and cardiovascular disease, lipids, inflammation, glucose metabolism, weight gain, infections, multiple sclerosis, mood, cognition, physical function and all-cause mortality, whereas intervention studies showed no effect of supplementation on disease occurrence; in 34 trials with 2805 individuals with mean baseline 25-hydroxyvitamin D below 50 nmol/L, 50 µg/day or more did not show better results. The authors propose that low 25-hydroxyvitamin D is a marker of ill health, lowered by inflammatory processes, rather than a cause.
